tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand what the Agentic Payments Environment is: a deterministic research sandbox for measuring and improving AI agent behavior on financial workflows. The document introduces the closed experimental loop (environment → tasks → agents → evals → failure taxonomy → rewards → optimization → report) and the headline metric—safe success rate—giving you the roadmap for everything that follows.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The `apenv` CLI in cli.py is the runtime front door, exposing subcommands like list, show, run, bench, replay, export, and annotate. Building on the README quick-start, this file shows how every experiment path—single episodes, full benchmarks, trace replay—enters the system through one command surface. The pyproject.toml manifest wires this module as the installed console script and declares runtime dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: Python packaging maps a console script name to a callable via `[project.scripts]` in pyproject.toml, so `apenv` resolves to `agentic_payments_env.cli:main` after `pip install -e .`.

tour.title: Domain Specification
tour.description: Before reading code, study docs/02-domain-model.md—the normative spec for money (int centavos, never floats), seeded identifiers, the simulated clock, transfer state machines, audit events, and world invariants. Every contract and tool implementation you encounter later must conform to these rules; violations here become catastrophic grading failures in the eval loop.

tour.title: Pydantic Contracts
tour.description: The contracts package defines the shared vocabulary as frozen Pydantic v2 models. common.py holds enums and validators; domain.py models accounts, transfers, and consents; actions.py defines tool calls and observations; tasks.py wraps TaskSpec with oracle plans and hidden ground truth. These types are the boundary between every layer—agents emit Actions, the environment returns Observations, graders consume EpisodeResults.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` with `ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid')` makes contracts immutable and rejects unknown fields—critical for deterministic replay and strict agent-environment handshakes.

tour.title: Environment Runtime
tour.description: PaymentsEnvironment in environment.py orchestrates the episode step loop: it holds WorldState, advances the simulated clock, injects faults from TaskSpec, and delegates each agent Action to the tool layer. This is the heart of the research instrument—everything an agent experiences flows through reset() and step(), making the environment the single authority on what is observable and what mutates state.

tour.title: Tool Dispatch Layer
tour.description: Building on the environment from Step 5, tools/dispatch.py routes each Action to its registered handler, wrapping failures as ToolError observations so bad agent calls never crash the run. tools/specs.py exposes ToolSpec definitions—names, descriptions, and JSON schemas—that agents (especially LLM agents) use to discover available operations. Together they form the agent's only interface to the banking world.
tour.languageLesson: The dispatcher pattern centralizes routing and error handling: handlers stay small and focused while dispatch.py guarantees every invalid tool name or argument returns a structured ToolError instead of raising.

tour.title: Transfer Policy Engine
tour.description: policies.py evaluates whether a proposed transfer satisfies consent, daily limits, night-window restrictions, and cooling-off rules before execution. The environment calls this engine during authorize and transfer tool handlers, so policy violations surface as observable errors the agent must recover from. Understanding these rules is essential for interpreting adversarial and policy-focused benchmark tasks.

tour.title: Agent Framework
tour.description: agents/base.py defines the Agent protocol—a single act() method that maps an Observation to an Action—shared by oracle, scripted, and LLM implementations. agents/llm.py is the production path: it converts observations to chat messages, calls a ChatModel adapter, and parses tool-call responses back into Action objects. The CLI's run and bench commands instantiate agents through presets, connecting this layer to the environment loop.
tour.languageLesson: Python Protocol classes (or ABCs) define structural typing for plug-in components: any class implementing act() qualifies as an Agent without inheriting a heavy base class.

tour.title: Graders and Taxonomy
tour.description: After an episode completes, graders score it across dimensions—safety, authorization, financial correctness, recovery, and more. graders/base.py defines the Grader interface; contracts/grading.py models Violation, DimensionResult, and EpisodeResult; graders/taxonomy.py maps violation codes to severity and dimension. The failure taxonomy is what turns raw traces into actionable research signals for optimization and reporting.

tour.title: Benchmark Runner
tour.description: benchmark/runner.py drives the full eval loop: load a TaskSpec, reset the environment, run the agent for up to max steps, grade the episode, and write trace and result artifacts. benchmark/loader.py routes task IDs to version-specific loaders (v0/v1) and serializes TaskSpec to JSON—the most depended-upon module in the graph. The CLI bench subcommand delegates here, making this the capstone integration of agents, environment, tools, policies, and graders.

tour.title: Reports and CI
tour.description: benchmark/report.py aggregates episode grading results into family summaries and renders Markdown benchmark reports—the final artifact in the experimental loop. The GitHub Actions CI workflow runs the full verification suite (ruff, mypy, pytest) on every push and pull request, ensuring the deterministic guarantees that make cross-run comparisons trustworthy. Together, reports produce evidence and CI guards reproducibility.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers for events, `jobs` for parallel work, and `steps` for sequential commands. Matrix builds across Python 3.11 and 3.12 catch version-specific regressions in a deterministic codebase.
